reason: While the text depicts the Hebrew people (Israelites) suffering greatly—pursued by Pharaoh's army with chariots—and complaining bitterly to Moses about their situation, Moses, their leader, does not blame them for their suffering. Instead, his response (Exodus 14:13-14) is one of reassurance: 'Do not be afraid. Stand firm and you will see the deliverance the Lord will bring you today... The Lord will fight for you.' Moses directs their attention to divine salvation rather than assigning fault to the people. The narrative attributes their plight to Pharaoh's pursuit and God's intervention, not to the people's failure.
story: The Pharaoh chases after the Hebrews
